title: node:sqlite
lede: Node's built-in node:sqlite module — a synchronous, dependency-free SQL database, backed by the system libsqlite3 (linked only when a program actually imports the module, the same posture fetch takes with libcurl). DatabaseSync and StatementSync block like fs.readFileSync, so there is no async/await: db.prepare(sql).all<Row>() runs the query and returns the rows. Result rows take their shape from an explicit call-site type argument (stmt.all<Row>() / stmt.get<Row>(), matching Node's own get<T>()/all<T>() typings), projected onto the query columns by name. Parameters bind positionally (?) or by name (a single object → :name/@name/$name); every column type round-trips, including BLOB → Uint8Array and INTEGER → bigint. You can register scalar user-defined functions with db.function(). Aggregate functions, session/changeset, extension loading, and async backup() are out of the current scope (the last three are rejected with a clear message, being absent from the system libsqlite3 or a native-plugin surface).

entries.name: new DatabaseSync(path, options?)
entries.signature: new DatabaseSync(path: string, options?: { readOnly?: boolean, open?: boolean, enableForeignKeyConstraints?: boolean, timeout?: number }): DatabaseSync
entries.description: Opens (or creates) a database. path may be a filename or ':memory:'. options is read from an object literal in V1: readOnly, open, enableForeignKeyConstraints (on by default → PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON), and timeout (→ sqlite3_busy_timeout).

entries.name: db.exec(sql)
entries.description: Runs one or more SQL statements with no result rows — schema, pragmas, and bulk DML. Throws a catchable Error on a SQL error.
entries.snippet: db.exec('CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)');

entries.name: db.prepare(sql)
entries.description: Compiles a SQL statement into a reusable StatementSync. Throws on a syntax error.
entries.snippet: const insert = db.prepare('INSERT INTO t (name) VALUES (?)');

entries.name: db.close() / db.isOpen
entries.description: Closes the database; isOpen reflects the open/closed state and reads false after close().

entries.name: db.open()
entries.description: Opens a connection constructed with { open: false } (or reopens after close()), reapplying the constructor's flags.
entries.snippet:
const db = new DatabaseSync('data.db', { open: false });
db.open();

entries.name: db.isTransaction
entries.description: True while a transaction is open (autocommit disabled).

returns.desc: Whether a transaction is in progress.

entries.name: db.location(dbName?)
entries.description: Returns the file backing the named database (default 'main'), or null for an in-memory/temporary database.

returns.desc: The backing file path, or null.

entries.name: db.function(name, fn)
entries.signature: function(name: string, options?: object, fn: (...args) => any): void
entries.description: Registers a scalar user-defined function callable from SQL. A per-registration trampoline converts each SQL argument to the closure's declared parameter type, invokes the compiled closure, and forwards the result. Parameter/return types must be number, integer, bigint, or string; aggregate functions and BLOB arguments are later stages.
entries.snippet:
db.function('shout', (s: string) => s.toUpperCase() + '!');
db.prepare('SELECT shout(name) FROM t').all<{ name: string }>();

entries.name: stmt.get<T>(...params)
entries.description: Runs the statement and returns the first row as a typed object, or null if there are none. The row shape T is given as an explicit type argument (or a resolvable named type); an untyped read is a compile error in V1.
entries.snippet: const row = db.prepare('SELECT id, name FROM t WHERE id = ?').get<{ id: number; name: string }>(1);

entries.name: stmt.all<T>(...params)
entries.description: Runs the statement and returns every row as a typed object array. Same explicit-row-type requirement as get<T>.
entries.snippet: const rows = db.prepare('SELECT id, name FROM t ORDER BY id').all<{ id: number; name: string }>();

entries.name: stmt.iterate<T>(...params)
entries.description: Iterates the result rows with for…of. Materialised eagerly in V1 (equivalent to all<T>()); a lazy .next() iterator is a later stage.
entries.snippet: for (const r of db.prepare('SELECT id FROM t').iterate<{ id: number }>()) sum += r.id;

entries.name: stmt.run(...params)
entries.description: Runs a write statement and returns the affected-row count and the last inserted rowid. Both are number in V1.

entries.name: stmt.columns()
entries.signature: columns(): { column, database, table, type, name }[]
entries.description: Returns one metadata object per result column. name (result name) and declared type are populated; origin column/table/database read null (they need SQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA, absent from the system libsqlite3).
entries.snippet: for (const c of stmt.columns()) console.log(c.name, c.type);

entries.name: stmt.sourceSQL / stmt.expandedSQL
entries.description: sourceSQL is the original SQL the statement was prepared from; expandedSQL renders it with the most recent bound parameter values inlined.

entries.name: stmt.setReadBigInts() / setAllowBareNamedParameters()
entries.signature: setReadBigInts(enabled: boolean): void; setAllowBareNamedParameters(enabled: boolean): void
entries.description: Accepted for API completeness but effectively no-ops: the statically-typed row field governs integer representation (declare a field bigint to read one), and bare named parameters are always accepted.

entries.name: Parameter binding (positional + named)
entries.description: Trailing positional arguments bind to ? placeholders; a single object argument binds named parameters (:name/@name/$name, or the bare key). An integral number binds as INTEGER, a fractional one as REAL, matching Node.
entries.snippet: db.prepare('SELECT * FROM t WHERE age > :min').all<Row>({ min: 40 });

entries.name: Column value mapping
entries.signature: INTEGER/REAL → number, TEXT → string, BLOB → Uint8Array, NULL → null
entries.description: Column values map to JS by storage class: INTEGER/REAL → number, TEXT → string, BLOB → Uint8Array, NULL → null. Type a field `T | null` to read a nullable column's NULL as null (a non-nullable field reads NULL as its zero); a `bigint`-typed field reads INTEGER as a bigint. A declared field with no matching result column throws.
entries.snippet:
const row = stmt.get<{ data: Uint8Array }>();
console.log(row?.data.length);

entries.name: Errors → catchable Error
entries.description: SQLite failures throw a catchable Error carrying message (sqlite3_errmsg), code ('ERR_SQLITE_ERROR'), a numeric errcode, and errstr — matching Node.
entries.snippet: try { db.prepare('SELECT * FROM missing').all<Row>(); } catch (e) { console.log((e as Error).message); }
